'''György Marx''' (25 May 1927 – 2 December 2002) was a Hungarian physicist, astrophysicist, science historian and professor. He discovered the [[lepton number]]s and established the [[Lepton number#Lepton flavor conservation|law of lepton flavor conservation]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=MT 2003/4 17 |url=http://www.matud.iif.hu/03apr/patkos.html |access-date=2023-12-08 |website=www.matud.iif.hu}}</ref><ref name="origo">{{cite web|url=http://www.origo.hu/tudomany/tarsadalom/20021219eltemettek.html|author=New Wave Media Group Zrt.|website=origo.hu|title=Eltemették Marx György fizikust <!--########## Eltemették Marx György fizikust - origo.hu #########--> |date=31 December 1899 |accessdate=2018-02-17}}</ref>

==Life==
He was the first non-[[British people|British]] laureate of the [[Lawrence Bragg Medal and Prize|Bragg Medal]]<ref>[http://www.iop.org/about/awards/gold/bragg/medallists/page_38631.html Bragg medal recipients] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180824065705/http://www.iop.org/about/awards/gold/bragg/medallists/page_38631.html |date=24 August 2018 }}, retrieved 2019-08-24.</ref> of the [[Institute of Physics]], in 2001. He received it for his "outstanding contributions to physics education".<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://wwwdfis.ts.infn.it/didatticaArchivio/Didattica/IFNS/dispense1011/nuclear_marx.pdf |title=Abstract - Life in the nuclear valley - George Marx |access-date=17 February 2018 |archive-date=18 February 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180218024119/http://wwwdfis.ts.infn.it/didatticaArchivio/Didattica/IFNS/dispense1011/nuclear_marx.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Marx authored a book about several of the 20th century's exceptional Hungarian scientists, ''The Voice of the Martians''.<ref name="Marx 2001 ">{{cite book | last=Marx | first=George | title=The voice of the Martians : Hungarian scientists who shaped the 20th century in the West | publisher=Akadémiai Kiadó | publication-place=Budapest | date=2001 | isbn=963-05-7830-1 | oclc=48621487 | page=}}</ref>

==Death==
[[File:Marx György sírja.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The tomb of György Marx and his parents in the [[Farkasréti Cemetery]] <small>(30/2-1-3.)</small>]]
Marx died on December 2, 2002, in Budapest after a serious illness. On December 18 he was buried at the [[Farkasréti Cemetery]] with [[Reformed Church in Hungary|Reformed]] ceremony in the presence of his family, friends, disciples, colleagues and fellow scientists. [[Szilveszter E. Vizi]], neuroscientist and president of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] said the prayer for him.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Origo |title=Eltemették Marx György fizikust |url=https://www.origo.hu/tudomany/20021219eltemettek.html |access-date=2023-12-08 |website=www.origo.hu/ |date=31 December 1899 |language=hu}}</ref>
